Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - token assumptions we can share

Hi David / Neha,

Thanks again for yesterday's workshop. As mentioned on the call, our finance team needs a tighter mapping from expected API patterns to $/month for the pilot so we can sign off internally. Specifically we want a short, auditable table showing:

- Typical prompt/response token counts for each endpoint (classify vs triage vs content-gen)
- Expected cache hit-rate assumptions and how those reduce effective tokens billed
- Batching latency tradeoffs we must accept (95p SLO) vs tokens/$ improvement
- Contingency for fallback to smaller quantized model if latency spikes or capacity dips

Can your team give us those numbers in a simple CSV and a 1-page explanation we can show finance? Our target close date is end of July; anything that shortens the finance review would be helpful.

I attached the MAP draft you sent — I've highlighted the sections our legal and procurement teams will read first.

Thanks,
Heather
Heather Alvarez
Head of AI Programs | NovaMed Health

Subject: Re: MAP - Token levers audit, cache/batching assumptions & close timeline

Heather —

Appreciate the clarity. We'll produce: (1) a token-econ CSV with per-endpoint median and 95p tokens, (2) a short rationale doc describing cache hit-rate sensitivity and batching assumptions, and (3) a stress scenario sheet showing cost delta if hit-rate swings +/-10% or if batching window grows from 10ms to 80ms.

Quick notes / asks for NovaMed to help make the numbers high-fidelity:
- Can you share a small representative traffic sample (anonymized) for 24–72h? Even request/response length distributions will materially tighten our sims.
- Any hard SLO targets for 95p latency — we used 600ms in the draft but that was placeholder.
- Do you expect persistent sessions with cached KV across calls (session stickiness)? If so, indicate typical session length in minutes.

Tentative timeline:
- Today (6/30): we generate first-pass CSV and stress sims (internal).
- 7/1: send CSV + 1p explanation to you for finance review.
- 7/6: incorporate your traffic sample and update sims.
- 7/9–7/12: sync with procurement/legal to clear contract/SLAs.
- Goal: final MAP + commercial term signature by 7/30.

I'll attach the first-pass CSV in this thread. Ben / Neha / Kim — please review the assumptions column and flag anything you think is optimistic.

—David
David Kim
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Subject: Re: MAP - Token levers audit, cache/batching assumptions & close timeline

David / team —

Quick pass from finance-facing angle after skimming the CSV: looks good but a few clarifying edits needed before we hand to NovaMed finance:

1) Token buckets: please break out "prompt tokens" vs "model context / KV tokens" vs "response tokens" in separate columns so their billing reconciliation is straightforward.

2) Cache assumptions: we should provide three hit-rate scenarios (low 15%, base 40%, high 65%) and show net tokens billed / 1M requests for each. Add a short note describing what counts as a cacheable prefix (single-turn vs multi-turn).

3) Batching: include an explicit column with assumed batch size and the inferred latency percentile changes. For example: batch window 25ms => 2x throughput, 95p latency +120ms.

4) Fallback quantization: show tokens/$ delta when using 4-bit quantized variant (quality delta flagged) and whether we'd route >=50% of tail requests to the quantized model under load.

I've annotated the CSV and uploaded a redlined one we can share directly with Heather if David agrees.

Ben / Kim: Ben, can you sanity-check the batching latency numbers? Kim, can you confirm whether our Dedicated plan has an automatic fallback knob we can guarantee in the MAP?

Thanks — I'll be on the 10am call to go over any finance questions.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Finance Partner, Growth Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Heather Alvarez <heather@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP - Token levers audit, cache/batching assumptions & close timeline

Neha / team —

Checked the batching latency sims against our latest runtime changes: the numbers in the CSV are conservative. A couple actionable clarifications I added:

- For batch window 25ms we see ~1.9–2.1x throughput on NVidia H100 and 1.6–1.8x on older A100s; I've put both ranges in the sheet.
- 95p latency increase depends heavily on payload shape — with short prompts (<64 tokens) the 95p delta is <100ms for 25ms batching; for long prompts (>512 tokens) it grows toward 250–300ms.
- Cache hit-rate sensitivity: our prefetch/KV warm strategy can raise effective hit-rate by ~8–12pp during steady-state for sessionized workloads; I added a column "prefetch uplift" to the CSV.
- Dedicated fallback: Kimberly confirmed we can automate failover to a quantized model variant and cap the % of routed requests; we'll include that as an operational flag in the MAP (defaults: 30% tail routing, configurable).

Heather — attaching the revised CSV and a 1-page explainer we can include in the MAP. If NovaMed can share the lightweight traffic sample David requested, we can lock these numbers down and shorten finance review.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
